The Derivatives of the Link-Scale Expected Information, Any Order

Source: R/d34expected_analytic.R
dexpected_link_higher.Rd

Applies Leibniz's rule and the diagonal Faa di Bruno formula to \(F_{ab}(\eta) = E_{ab}(\theta(\eta))\,h_a'(\eta_a)\,h_b'(\eta_b)\), at orders one to four.

Usage

dexpected_link_higher(params, nat, h, order)

Arguments

params

The parameter names.

nat

A list: nat[[1]] the expected information on the parameter scale, keyed as hess_names(), and nat[[m + 1]] its derivatives of order m, keyed as dexpected_names(), d2expected_names(), d3expected_names() and d4expected_names().

h

The inverse link's derivatives, from inverse_link_derivs(), to order order + 1.

order

1L to 4L.

Value

A named list on the link scale, keyed as the order's names.

Details

For a multiset \(S\) of coordinates, with \(G_{ab} = E_{ab}\circ\theta\) and \(u_{ab} = h_a' h_b'\), $$\partial_S F_{ab} = \sum_{T \subseteq S} \binom{S}{T}\, \partial_T G_{ab}\;\partial_{S \setminus T} u_{ab},$$ where the sum runs over the sub-multisets of \(S\) and the coefficient is the product over the distinct indices of the binomial coefficients of their multiplicities. Each parameter moves with its own coordinate only, so $$\partial_T G_{ab} = \sum_{j} \partial^{J} E_{ab} \prod_i B_{m_i, j_i}(h_i', h_i'', \dots),$$ with \(m_i\) the multiplicity of index \(i\) in \(T\), \(1 \le j_i \le m_i\), \(J\) the multiset holding each \(i\) \(j_i\) times, and \(B\) the partial Bell polynomials of bell_partial(). The factor \(\partial_R u_{ab}\) vanishes unless \(R\) names only \(a\) and \(b\); then it is \(h_a^{(1+r_a)} h_b^{(1+r_b)}\) for \(a \ne b\) and \(\sum_k \binom{r}{k} h_a^{(1+k)} h_a^{(1+r-k)}\) for \(a = b\).
